subject: pathology
title: Trinucleotide Repeat Diseases, Genetic Anticipation, and Fragile X Syndrome

steps.tx: Certain inherited neurological and neuromuscular disorders depart from standard Mendelian rules due to dynamic mutations characterized by unstable expansions of repetitive three-nucleotide sequences. During parent gametogenesis, DNA replication slippage expands these unstable repeats, defining the dynamic mutational mechanism of **trinucleotide repeat expansion**.
steps.say: Trinucleotide repeat expansions are dynamic mutations that expand during gametogenesis.

Intermediate Premutation Allele Becomes Meiotically Unstable
Strand Slippage During DNA Polymerase Meiotic Replication
Massive Triplet Expansion Manifests as Overt Clinical Disease

steps.tx: As unstable triplet repeats expand progressively across successive generations within an affected family pedigree, clinical symptoms appear at an earlier age and express with increasing phenotypic severity. This classic non-Mendelian generational acceleration and worsening of disease is known as **genetic anticipation**.
steps.say: Genetic anticipation describes the earlier onset and greater severity of disease in successive generations.

left.title: Classic Static Mendelian Mutation
points: Point mutation or deletion remains identical in size across generations
Consistent age of clinical disease onset among affected family members
Recurrence risk adheres strictly to constant 50% or 25% Mendelian ratios
No generational acceleration of disease severity or organ involvement

right.title: Dynamic Trinucleotide Expansion
points: Triplet repeat copy number increases progressively during meiosis
Manifests progressive genetic anticipation with earlier onset in offspring
Severity of clinical phenotype correlates directly with repeat tract length
Parental sex of transmission dictates expansion propensity

steps.tx: The most common inherited form of intellectual disability in biological males arises from dynamic CGG triplet expansion in the 5-prime untranslated region of the FMR1 gene on chromosome Xq27.3. Characterized by macroorchidism, long face, large everted ears, and autistic features, this disorder is **fragile X syndrome**.
steps.say: Fragile X syndrome is caused by CGG triplet expansion in FMR1, causing intellectual disability.

vis.alt: FMR1 CGG repeat expansion and transcriptional silencing in Fragile X
vis.caption: CGG repeat expansion leading to hypermethylation and silencing of the FMR1 gene.

steps.tx: In fragile X syndrome, expansion beyond two hundred CGG repeats triggers extensive DNA hypermethylation of adjacent CpG islands in the FMR1 promoter. Transcriptional silencing abolishes synthesis of fragile X mental retardation protein, an RNA-binding chaperone required for synaptic pruning, during **FMR1 epigenetic silencing**.
steps.say: Hypermethylation of expanded CGG repeats silences FMR1, abolishing FMRP synthesis.

nodes.label: CGG Triplet Repeats Expand Beyond 200 in Maternal Oogenesis
DNA Methyltransferases Hypermethylate Cytosines in Promoter
Heterochromatin Formation Shuts Down FMR1 Gene Transcription
Absence of FMRP Impairs Dendritic Spine Synaptic Pruning

steps.tx: Huntington disease represents the prototypic polyglutamine trinucleotide repeat disorder. Autosomal dominant CAG repeat expansion in the coding exon of the HTT gene on chromosome 4p16.3 produces a mutant huntingtin protein that aggregates within medium spiny striatal neurons, causing chorea and dementia in **Huntington disease**.
steps.say: Huntington disease is a CAG polyglutamine disorder causing selective caudate striatal atrophy.

vis.alt: Huntington disease neuropathology showing caudate and putamen atrophy
vis.caption: Bilateral atrophy of the caudate nucleus and putamen resulting from mutant huntingtin neurotoxicity.

steps.tx: Paternal transmission of the mutant HTT allele during male spermatogenesis exhibits marked instability, resulting in dramatic CAG expansions in offspring. Inheriting high repeat numbers exceeding sixty CAG repeats precipitates juvenile-onset Huntington disease, an illustration of **paternal anticipation in Huntington**, causing early chorea and rigidity.
steps.say: CAG repeats expand predominantly during paternal spermatogenesis, accelerating disease onset.

nodes.label: Unstable CAG Triplet Slippage During Male Spermatogenesis
CAG Repeat Count Jumps Dramatically from 45 to Over 70
Presents with Severe Rigidity, Seizures, and Death in Adolescence

steps.tx: The most common adult muscular dystrophy results from CTG repeat expansion in the 3-prime untranslated region of the DMPK gene on chromosome 19q13.3. Characterized by sustained muscle contraction after voluntary movement, frontal balding, cataracts, and testicular atrophy, this disorder is **myotonic dystrophy**.
steps.say: Myotonic dystrophy involves CTG expansion in DMPK, causing impaired muscle relaxation and cataracts.

steps.tx: Distinct from triplet expansions, certain genomic loci undergo parent-of-origin specific epigenetic inactivation through differential DNA methylation. This selective transcriptional silencing of either the maternal or paternal allele represents **genomic imprinting**, ensuring that only one functional parental allele is expressed in diploid cells.
steps.say: Genomic imprinting silences either the maternal or paternal allele via parent-specific DNA methylation.
